segments.text: Pretend you're a scribe in the 1450s.
You hand copy proclamations all day.
Steady job.
Then you hear a guy built a machine that prints pages
a thousand times faster than you can write them.
You face two choices.
Pretend it isn't happening, or learn to run it.
The math is simple.
Run the machine, or someone else will take your place.
AI isn't a futuristic destination you go visit.
It moved from science fiction into normal life
in just a few years, and it is already running
inside the tools your first job will hand you on day one.
This board shows where AI is already integrated
into your day.
On the left, we have the recommends category.
When Spotify, Netflix, or TikTok predict
what you might like next, they are using AI
to make those choices.
Next is navigation.
Tools like Google Maps or Waze use AI
to analyze traffic patterns and calculate your arrival time.
Then there's face recognition.
When you unlock your phone by looking at it,
or an app tags your friends in a photo,
an AI system is checking to see if those faces match.
Voice assistants like Siri, Alexa, and Google use AI
to turn the sound you make into written words.
And finally, chat bots.
Programs like Chat GPT, Claude, and Gemini
use AI to hold conversations and answer your questions.
AI was already part of your daily routine
long before these conversational chat bots arrived.
The great news is you do not have to wait until college
or your first career to build these skills.
You can start practicing right now.
Consider graphic design.
Before personal computers, becoming a designer
meant spending years at a drafting table,
mastering techniques entirely by hand.
Then desktop publishing put powerful design tools
right on a teenager's desk.
They could create professional posters,
magazines, and brochures
while developing their eye for layout.
The software did not replace design skill.
It simply shortened the distance
between wanting to do the work
and actually getting it done.
You are perfectly positioned to take advantage
of this shift by building foundational habits today.
This chart outlines three reasons you'll thrive.
First, this is your time.
While you are in school, you have the ideal sandbox
to try new things, ask questions,
and learn from what happens.
Second, you will move faster.
AI gives you immediate feedback
and helps you tackle complex projects
you wouldn't have known how to start otherwise.
You learn by building.
Third, you build good habits early.
You get to practice asking precise questions,
verifying the answers you receive
and making your own independent decisions.
Start now and you build a permanent, adaptable skillset
that you will carry straight
into whatever industry comes next.
AI fits into a long historical pattern.
It isn't the first technology to rewrite how we work.
The steam engine took over massive amounts
of raw physical labor
and electricity revolutionized
how factories produced goods.
Later, the internet completely rewrote
how humanity accesses and shares information.
While previous inventions only automated
specific domains and narrow tasks,
AI has the capacity to scale
across almost everything simultaneously.
In July 2025, the White House released
an official national strategy document titled,
Winning the Race, America's AI Action Plan.
The document describes the technology's potential this way,
an industrial revolution, an information revolution,
and a renaissance all at once.
This is the potential that AI presents.
AI is today's printing press.
Learn to run it.
